transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Yeah, um, what brings me in... well, what finally scared me into coming in is that I keep making these just... really dumb technical mistakes at work. Things I absolutely know better than to make. 

I've been a camera operator and editor for a long time—I actually went to film school in Chicago, which, by the way, I do not recommend in the winter. I don't know if you've ever been there in February, but the wind coming off the lake literally feels like it’s slicing your face off. We had to shoot this outdoor documentary project once and my hands were so numb I almost dropped a very expensive prime lens in the snow... 

But anyway, sorry. The mistakes. Lately I'm just doing things like labeling camera cards wrong, or I'll completely miss a timecode note from the director. I even exported a client cut the other day with the wrong lower-third graphic on the screen, and the crazy part is I did that even after I had just checked it. The client was this boutique pet food brand—they make these organic treats for dogs with poultry allergies, which is wild to me, but I guess dogs get allergies too, and it reminds me I actually need to buy food for my sister's pug later... 

But yeah, sending out a final cut with an error like that when I *knew* I checked it... it really freaked me out.
Have you always struggled with these kinds of focus issues and careless mistakes throughout your life, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

Oh, no, it's definitely not new. I mean, even back in elementary school... I remember my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she actually had to move my desk right up next to hers. I was always just up and out of my seat, or I'd be blurting out the answers before she even finished asking the question. Or I'd be bothering the kids next to me before I even realized I was doing it. 

I used to sit next to this kid named Kevin, who had this giant collection of those scented markers? The Mr. Sketch ones? Oh my gosh, the blue one smelled exactly like blue raspberry, which is funny because blue raspberries don't even exist in nature, right? It's just a flavor they made up for ice pops so you wouldn't confuse it with cherry or strawberry. I actually watched a mini-doc about flavor scientists once, and it's wild how they synthesize that stuff in a lab. I've always wanted to shoot a project in a food lab, the lighting with all the glass beakers would look so cool on camera... 

But yeah, Kevin got so mad because I kept grabbing his markers without asking. Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, if this is a new thing. No, I guess I've kind of always been like this.
Beyond these issues with focus and restlessness, have you felt consistently down, sad, or hopeless for most days over the past two years or more?

No, I wouldn't say I've felt down or hopeless. I mean, frustrated? Definitely. But not sad. I actually consider myself a pretty upbeat person. Like, even when things go wrong on set, I'm usually the one trying to keep the energy up. 

I worked on this one indie feature a couple of years ago, and everything that could go wrong did. The lead actor got food poisoning from the craft services table—which, by the way, I told the producer you can't just leave potato salad sitting out in the sun for four hours. It was a nightmare. We were shooting out in the desert, near Joshua Tree, and the heat was just oppressive. Have you ever been out there? It's beautiful, but it's like being inside an oven. The rocks look like they were stacked by giants, though. I got some incredible b-roll footage of the sunset hitting those rocks. It turns this crazy shade of orange, almost like a tangerine. I actually painted my living room that color last year. Well, one accent wall. I started painting the whole room but then I realized it was way too bright, so I had to go back to Home Depot like three times to find the right neutral tone to balance it out... 

But anyway, no, I don't feel depressed or hopeless. Just... really annoyed with myself lately for messing up at work.
Outside of your work environment, do you often find yourself losing things or forgetting about daily errands and appointments?

Um, losing things? Oh, definitely. All the time. My keys, my phone, my sunglasses... I actually lost a really expensive pair of Ray-Bans last summer when I went to this music festival. It was one of those three-day outdoor things, you know? The lineup was amazing, but the dust was just unbelievable. I was blowing dirt out of my nose for a week. We were camping, which I usually love, but our tent was pitched right next to this group of guys who decided to play acoustic guitar at 3 AM every single night. Like, I appreciate Wonderwall as much as the next person, but come on. And then on the second day, I went to get some food from this taco truck—best al pastor I've ever had, by the way, they put this grilled pineapple salsa on it that was just incredible. I actually tried to recreate it at home, but I couldn't get the char on the pineapple quite right. I think I need one of those indoor grill pans. Cast iron, probably. My mom has this vintage Le Creuset one that she never uses, I should really ask her if I can borrow it... 

But yeah, I set my sunglasses down on the little ledge by the taco truck window to get my wallet out, and when I turned back around, they were just gone. So annoying. And errands? Yeah, I'm terrible at that. I'll go to the store for three things, walk out with two bags of stuff I didn't need, and completely forget the main thing I went for. It's a running joke with my friends at this point.
Do you still find yourself feeling physically restless or needing to move around frequently, even when you are in situations where you are expected to sit still for long periods?

Oh, yeah, absolutely. Sitting still is torture. Like, if I'm in a client screening and we're watching a rough cut? It feels like there's this actual physical pressure building up under my skin. Like my body is just screaming at me to get up and do something, even though I know I'm supposed to just sit there quietly and take notes. 

We had this one screening last month for a documentary about urban beekeeping. Which, by the way, is fascinating. Did you know bees recognize human faces? It's true! I read this whole article about how they process visual information, and it's completely different from how we do it. They see ultraviolet light, so flowers look totally different to them. Like they have little landing strips painted on them that we can't even see. I really want to get one of those UV lenses for my camera and do a whole macro photography series on local flora. There's this botanical garden near my apartment that has the most incredible orchids. Orchids are so finicky, though. I bought one from Trader Joe's once, and it died in like three days. I think I overwatered it. You're supposed to just give them an ice cube once a week, right? I always forget the ice cube thing. 

But yeah, during that screening, I was bouncing my leg so much the client actually asked if there was an earthquake. I was so embarrassed. I just can't just sit there. I have to be doing something.
